parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/app.module.ts is the NestJS root module. The layer model puts it in presentation because of the **/*.module.ts pattern. The file only wires the application together: it loads configuration with ConfigModule.forRoot, sets up the database connection with TypeOrmModule.forRoot, registers the entity classes and imports DeliveryModule. This is ordinary composition-root work for a NestJS module file. It sets connection options but contains no persistence logic such as queries, repositories or transactions, and no business rules or domain computations. The file has no executable logic beyond the setup passed to the @Module decorator. Writing database settings inline instead of using an infrastructure-level provider such as TypeOrmModule.forRootAsync with a config factory is a code-hygiene concern, not a misplaced layer responsibility. The 'synchronize: true' setting carries some risk, but that is also not a layer-role violation. The confidence is moderate because a stricter reading could count the inline TypeORM connection setup as persistence configuration that belongs in the infrastructure layer.
